# Third-Party MCP Servers: Installation and Configuration

This document explains how to install and configure the native MCP servers used for benchmarking. These are the third-party alternatives the benchmark compares Airbyte Agents against.

The benchmark's `native-mcp` path uses recordings captured from these providers' MCP tools. To capture fresh recordings or independently verify tool call shapes, you need access to these servers.

## Overview

Each connector in the benchmark has a corresponding MCP server maintained by the service provider (or the MCP open-source project):

| Connector | MCP Server | Transport | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linear | `https://mcp.linear.app/mcp` | Streamable HTTP (remote) | OAuth 2.0 (browser flow) or API key |
| Slack | `https://mcp.slack.com/mcp` | Streamable HTTP (remote) | OAuth 2.0 (user token) |
| Zendesk | `ghcr.io/dunialabs/mcp-servers/zendesk` | stdio (local, via Docker) | OAuth access token |
| Gong | `kenazk/gong-mcp` | stdio (local, via Node.js) | Basic (access key + secret) |
| Salesforce | `api.salesforce.com/platform/mcp` | SSE (remote) | OAuth 2.0 (refresh token) |

Linear, Slack, and Salesforce all run as remote hosted servers. Linear uses browser-based OAuth; Slack and Salesforce use OAuth 2.0 with a custom app (a Slack app and a Salesforce Connected App, respectively). Zendesk runs locally via Docker with an OAuth access token.

---

## Linear MCP

Linear provides an official remote MCP server at `https://mcp.linear.app/mcp`. It follows the authenticated remote MCP spec with OAuth 2.0 and dynamic client registration.

**Docs:** https://linear.app/docs/mcp

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http linear-server https://mcp.linear.app/mcp
```

Then open a Claude Code session, run `/mcp`, select the Linear server, and complete the OAuth flow in your browser.

### Claude Desktop

Navigate to Settings > Connectors, search for Linear, and connect. Available on Team and Enterprise plans. On other paid plans, use Settings > Connectors in the Claude desktop app.

### Other MCP Clients (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.)

For clients that do not support remote MCP natively, use `mcp-remote` as a bridge:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "linear": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.linear.app/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

### API Key Auth (Non-Interactive)

Linear also supports passing an API key directly via the `Authorization: Bearer` header instead of the interactive OAuth flow. Generate a key from Linear > Settings > Account > Security & Access > API Keys.

### Available Tools

The benchmark uses these Linear MCP tools (tool names as they appear in Claude Code):

| Benchmark Task | Tool | Example Args |
|---|---|---|
| search | `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_issues` | `{"query": "context store", "limit": 10}` |
| get | `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__get_issue` | `{"id": "AGENTIC-338"}` |
| list | `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_issues` | `{"limit": 50}` |

The Linear MCP server also provides tools for creating and updating issues, managing projects, and more. Only the read tools are relevant to this benchmark.

---

## Slack MCP

The benchmark uses Slack's official hosted MCP server at `https://mcp.slack.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0, OAuth 2.0). Authenticating requires creating a Slack app in your workspace, enabling the Model Context Protocol toggle, adding User Token Scopes, and minting a User OAuth Token (`xoxp-...`).

**Slack official docs:** https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server

### Prerequisites

- A Slack workspace where you can create or manage apps
- Permission to install/reinstall the app in that workspace

### Step 1: Create a Slack App

1. Go to https://api.slack.com/apps
2. Click "Create New App" > "From scratch"
3. Name your app (e.g., "agent-bench-mcp") and select your workspace

### Step 2: Enable Model Context Protocol

1. In the app settings sidebar under **Features**, open the **Agents & AI Apps** page
2. Find the **Model Context Protocol** card (it is below the "Agent or Assistant" card) and toggle it **on**
3. Save if prompted

> **Watch out:** the same page also has a separate **Agent or Assistant** toggle near the top. That is *not* the MCP toggle — flipping it has no effect on `mcp.slack.com/mcp` and you'll still get `App is not enabled for Slack MCP server access` errors. The **Model Context Protocol** toggle is in its own card further down the page.

### Step 3: Add User Token Scopes

The hosted MCP requires *user* token scopes (not bot scopes — bot tokens are not accepted). Navigate to **OAuth & Permissions** > **User Token Scopes** and add:

- `search:read.public` — search public channel content
- `search:read.private` — search private channel content
- `search:read.users` — search users by name/email/profile attributes
- `users:read` — read workspace member directory
- `users:read.email` — read member email addresses

(Slack's umbrella `search:read` scope also covers the three `search:read.*` entries; either choice works.)

### Step 4: Install and Get the User OAuth Token

1. Sidebar > **Install App** > click **Install to Workspace** (or **Reinstall to Workspace** if you've changed scopes)
2. Approve the consent screen
3. Copy the **User OAuth Token** at the top of the page — it starts with `xoxp-...`

> **Watch out:** any time you change scopes or toggle MCP on/off, you must **reinstall** the app for the existing tokens to pick up the new capability. A token minted before MCP was enabled will continue to return `App is not enabled for Slack MCP server access` until you reinstall.

### Step 4b: Verify the Token Works

Quick smoke test before wiring it into the recorder:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://mcp.slack.com/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_USER_OAUTH_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"smoke","version":"0.1"}}}'
```

A successful response includes `"serverInfo":{"name":"Slack MCP",...}` and a `mcp-session-id` header. Common failures:

| Error | Cause |
|---|---|
| `missing_token` | `Authorization` header not sent or empty |
| `App is not enabled for Slack MCP server access` | MCP toggle off, or app not reinstalled after enabling |
| `invalid_auth` | Token revoked, app uninstalled, or token from a different workspace |

### Step 5: Configure the Recorder

Add the token to your `.env` profile:

```
SLACK_USER_OAUTH_TOKEN=xoxp-...
```

The recorder reads only from `.env` (see `.env.template` for the full list of credential fields). If you keep credentials in 1Password, store this one under the `slack` item, section `test-credentials-mcp`, field `user_oauth_token`, and run `agent-bench populate-env` to sync it down to `.env`.

### Available Tools

The benchmark exercises two of the hosted MCP's tools:

| MCP Server Tool | Benchmark Tool | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `slack_search_channels` | `mcp__slack__slack_search_channels` | Search channels by name/description (cursor-paginated, max 20/call). Used by `slack-search` and the search-then-filter fallback for `slack-get`. |
| `slack_search_users` | `mcp__slack__slack_search_users` | Search users by name, email, or profile attributes (cursor-paginated, max 20/call). Used by `slack-user-search`. |

Notable limitations of the hosted MCP:

- **No get-channel-by-ID tool.** The `slack-get` scenario has no clean native counterpart and falls back to a search-then-filter approximation in the planner.
- Search results are capped at 20 per call across both `slack_search_channels` and `slack_search_users`.

The hosted MCP also exposes message-search, channel-read, thread-read, canvas, and chat-write tools (gated by `channels:history`, `chat:write`, `canvases:*`, etc.) — the benchmark does not use them today.

---

## Zendesk MCP

The benchmark uses the community **dunialabs/mcp-zendesk** server (TypeScript, MIT, Docker image) via stdio transport. No official Zendesk MCP server exists.

**Repo:** https://github.com/dunialabs/mcp-servers/tree/main/mcp-zendesk
**Docker image:** `ghcr.io/dunialabs/mcp-servers/zendesk:latest`

### Prerequisites

- Docker
- A Zendesk instance with an OAuth client configured (Admin Center > Apps > APIs > OAuth clients)

### Environment Variables

The recording script prefers environment variables from the active `.env` profile, falling back to 1Password (`zendesk-support` item, `test-credentials-oauth` section). Set these in your `.env` profile:

```bash
ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN=your-subdomain
ZENDESK_ACCESS_TOKEN=[REDACTED]
ZENDESK_REFRESH_TOKEN=[REDACTED]
ZENDESK_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
ZENDESK_CLIENT_SECRET=[REDACTED]
ZENDESK_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:8080/callback
```

See `.env.template` for the full list of credential fields.

### Obtaining OAuth Tokens

The Zendesk MCP Docker container requires an OAuth access token. Tokens expire every 30 minutes, so you will need to refresh or re-authorize periodically.

**Step 1: Start a local callback server**

Start a simple HTTP server on the port that matches your `ZENDESK_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI`:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8080 &
```

Or use a script that captures the authorization code from the `?code=` query parameter.

**Step 2: Open the authorization URL in a browser**

```
https://<ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN>.zendesk.com/oauth/authorizations/new?\
  response_type=code&\
  client_id=<ZENDESK_CLIENT_ID>&\
  redirect_uri=<ZENDESK_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI>&\
  scope=read
```

> **Important:** The `redirect_uri` must exactly match one of the allowed redirect URIs configured on the OAuth client in Zendesk Admin Center (Apps > APIs > OAuth clients). Using a non-allowed URI will fail silently or return an error. Check the client configuration if the flow does not redirect.

**Step 3: Exchange the authorization code for tokens**

```bash
curl -X POST "https://<ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN>.zendesk.com/oauth/tokens" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "grant_type": "authorization_code",
    "code": "<AUTH_CODE>",
    "client_id": "<ZENDESK_CLIENT_ID>",
    "client_secret": "[REDACTED]",
    "redirect_uri": "<ZENDESK_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI>",
    "scope": "read"
  }'
```

The response includes `access_token` and `refresh_token`. Save both to your `.env` file immediately — Zendesk rotates the refresh token on every use, so the old one becomes invalid.

**Step 4: Refresh an expired token**

Access tokens expire after 30 minutes. Refresh them programmatically using the
credentials already in your `.env` file:

```bash
source .env   # loads ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN, ZENDESK_CLIENT_ID, etc.

curl -s -X POST "https://${ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN}.zendesk.com/oauth/tokens" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{
    \"grant_type\": \"refresh_token\",
    \"client_id\": \"${ZENDESK_CLIENT_ID}\",
    \"client_secret\": \"${ZENDESK_CLIENT_SECRET}\",
    \"refresh_token\": \"${ZENDESK_REFRESH_TOKEN}\",
    \"scope\": \"read\"
  }"
```

The response contains both a new `access_token` and a new `refresh_token`:

```json
{
  "access_token": "...",
  "refresh_token": "...",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "expires_in": 1799,
  "scope": "read",
  "refresh_token_expires_in": 2591999
}
```

> **Warning — token rotation:** Zendesk invalidates the previous refresh token
> on every use. You *must* update **both** `ZENDESK_ACCESS_TOKEN` and
> `ZENDESK_REFRESH_TOKEN` in your `.env` file immediately after each refresh.
> The recorder reads `ZENDESK_ACCESS_TOKEN` on every native-mcp run, so
> leaving the old value will cause a 401 even though the refresh succeeded.
> If you lose the new refresh token (e.g., by running the refresh again with
> the old token), you must redo the full browser authorization flow from
> Step 1.

### How the Recording Script Launches It

The `ZendeskMCP` class in `src/agent_bench/recording/native_mcp_recorder.py` launches the Docker container with stdio transport:

```bash
docker run -i --rm \
  -e zendeskSubdomain=$ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN \
  -e accessToken=[REDACTED] \
  ghcr.io/dunialabs/mcp-servers/zendesk:latest
```

The container reads JSON-RPC messages from stdin and writes responses to stdout.

### Available Tools

| Benchmark Task | MCP Tool | Args | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| search | `zendeskSearchTickets` | `{"query": "sync"}` | Search tickets using Zendesk query syntax |
| get | `zendeskGetTicket` | `{"ticket_id": 2}` | Retrieve a single ticket by ID |
| list | `zendeskListTickets` | `{}` | List recent tickets (default 25) |

The server exposes 18 tools total (ticket, user, and organization management). The benchmark uses only the three ticket read operations listed above.

---

## Salesforce MCP

Salesforce provides official hosted MCP servers at `api.salesforce.com`. The benchmark uses the **SObject Reads** server, which supports read-only SOQL queries and SOSL searches.

**Docs:** https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/guide/client-connection-overview.html
**Server reference:** https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/references/reference/servers-reference.html

### Server URL

```
https://api.salesforce.com/platform/mcp/v1/platform/sobject-reads
```

### Prerequisites

- A Salesforce org with API access enabled (production, not Developer Edition)
- An External Client App configured for MCP access (see below)
- OAuth credentials: `consumer_key` (client ID), `consumer_secret`, and a `refresh_token`

### Key Details for Airbyte's Salesforce Org

- **Org domain:** `airbyte.my.salesforce.com` (always use this, never `login.salesforce.com`)
- **MCP Home:** `https://airbyte.my.salesforce-setup.com/lightning/setup/McpServer/home`
- **External Client App config:** `https://airbyte.my.salesforce-setup.com/lightning/setup/ManageExternalClientApplication/0xIUJ0000000cA9/detail`
- **App name:** "Salesforce MCP (Internal Access)" (stored in 1Password `direct-connector-credentials` vault, `salesforce` item, section `test-credentials-mcp`)
- **Callback URL configured in the app:** `https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback`

### Authentication

The benchmark authenticates via the OAuth 2.0 refresh token flow. The recording script exchanges the refresh token for an access token at `https://airbyte.my.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token`, then passes the access token as a `Bearer` token to the MCP server.

**Required environment variables:**

```bash
export SF_MCP_CONSUMER_KEY="your-connected-app-consumer-key"
export SF_MCP_CONSUMER_SECRET="[REDACTED]"
export SF_MCP_REFRESH_TOKEN="[REDACTED]"
```

These are set in your `.env` profile (e.g., `.env.dallas-prod`). Consumer key and secret are also available from 1Password (`salesforce` item, section `test-credentials-mcp`).

### Setting Up an External Client App

Salesforce recommends **External Client Apps** (not legacy Connected Apps) for MCP connections. To create one:

1. Follow the [Salesforce MCP setup guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/guide/create-external-client-app.html)
2. Set the callback URL to match your MCP client (e.g., `https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback` for Claude)
3. The app will be assigned a **Consumer Key** and **Consumer Secret** automatically

> **Important:** External Client Apps require PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) for the authorization code flow. You must include `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method=S256` parameters in the authorize URL, and `code_verifier` in the token exchange.

### Obtaining a Refresh Token

After creating the External Client App, generate a refresh token via the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE:

**Step 1: Generate a PKCE code verifier and challenge:**

```python
import secrets, hashlib, base64

verifier = secrets.token_urlsafe(64)
challenge = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(
    hashlib.sha256(verifier.encode()).digest()
).rstrip(b"=").decode()
print(f"VERIFIER={verifier}")
print(f"CHALLENGE={challenge}")
```

Save these values — you need the verifier for the token exchange in Step 4.

**Step 2: Open the authorize URL in your browser:**

Replace `YOUR_CONSUMER_KEY` and `YOUR_CHALLENGE` with your values:

```
https://airbyte.my.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=YOUR_CONSUMER_KEY&redirect_uri=https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback&code_challenge=YOUR_CHALLENGE&code_challenge_method=S256
```

> **Important:** Always use the org-specific domain (`airbyte.my.salesforce.com`), never `login.salesforce.com`. Using `login.salesforce.com` may route to the wrong org or fail with `redirect_uri_mismatch`.

> **Important:** The `redirect_uri` must exactly match the callback URL configured in the External Client App. For Airbyte's app, this is `https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback`.

> **Important:** Do not pass explicit `scope` parameters. External Client Apps use pre-configured scopes. Passing `scope=api+refresh_token` will fail with `invalid_scope`. The app's configured scopes (`refresh_token mcp_api`) are applied automatically.

**Step 3: Log in and authorize the app.** After authorization, the browser redirects to the callback URL with an authorization code in the query string:

```
https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback?code=AUTH_CODE_HERE
```

Claude's server may show an error (missing `state` parameter) — that's fine. Copy the `code` value from the URL before the page finishes loading.

**Step 4: Exchange the authorization code for tokens:**

```bash
curl -X POST https://airbyte.my.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token \
  -d "grant_type=authorization_code" \
  -d "client_id=YOUR_CONSUMER_KEY" \
  -d "client_secret=[REDACTED]" \
  -d "redirect_uri=https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback" \
  -d "code=AUTH_CODE_HERE" \
  -d "code_verifier=YOUR_VERIFIER"
```

The response includes `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `instance_url`, and `scope`. Save the `refresh_token` to your `.env` profile as `SF_MCP_REFRESH_TOKEN`.

### Troubleshooting

- **`redirect_uri_mismatch`**: The `redirect_uri` in the authorize URL must exactly match what's configured in the External Client App. Check the app config page linked above.
- **`invalid_scope`**: Do not pass `scope` parameter for External Client Apps. Scopes are pre-configured in the app.
- **`app_not_found`**: The External Client App is not installed in the Salesforce org you're authenticating against. Make sure you're using `airbyte.my.salesforce.com`, not a Developer Edition org like `airbyte-dev-ed`.
- **`missing required code_challenge`**: External Client Apps require PKCE. Include `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method=S256` in the authorize URL.
- **401 from hosted MCP endpoint**: The access token must come from a production org with MCP access enabled. Developer Edition orgs (`airbyte-dev-ed`) do not have access to `api.salesforce.com/platform/mcp`.

### How the Recording Script Uses It

The `SalesforceMCP` class in `src/agent_bench/recording/native_mcp_recorder.py` connects to the hosted MCP server using Streamable HTTP transport:

1. Exchanges the refresh token for an access token via `airbyte.my.salesforce.com`
2. Sends a JSON-RPC `initialize` request to the MCP server URL
3. Receives an `mcp-session-id` header for subsequent requests
4. Calls tools via JSON-RPC `tools/call` requests with the session header

### Claude Desktop / Claude Code

Salesforce hosted MCP servers support native OAuth with Claude. Add via Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http salesforce-reads https://api.salesforce.com/platform/mcp/v1/platform/sobject-reads
```

Then complete the OAuth flow in your browser when prompted. See [Salesforce's Claude configuration guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/guide/configure-claude.html) for details.

### Other MCP Clients (Cursor, Postman, etc.)

For clients that support OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, point them at the server URL and your External Client App's consumer key. Salesforce has tested with Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and Postman. See the [client connection overview](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/guide/client-connection-overview.html) for per-client instructions.

### Available Tools

The benchmark uses the SObject Reads server, which exposes these tools:

| Benchmark Task | MCP Tool | Example Args | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| search | `find` | `{"q": "FIND {airbyte} IN ALL FIELDS RETURNING Account(Id, Name, Type, Industry LIMIT 10)"}` | SOSL search across objects |
| get | `soqlQuery` | `{"q": "SELECT Id, Name, Type, Industry FROM Account WHERE Id = '0015e00000FMsFhAAL'"}` | SOQL query for a single record |

The benchmark records these as `mcp__salesforce__find` and `mcp__salesforce__soqlQuery` in the recording files.

Notable behavior:

- The SObject Reads server is read-only. For write operations, use the SObject All or SObject Mutations servers instead.
- SOSL `FIND` queries search across all indexed fields. Results depend on the org's search index state.
- SOQL `SELECT` queries respect the org's field-level security and sharing rules.
- The server uses Streamable HTTP with session IDs. Each `initialize` handshake returns an `mcp-session-id` header that must be included in subsequent requests.
- Rate limits follow Salesforce's standard API limits for the org edition.

---

## Using These Servers With the Benchmark

### Viewing Results Without Recording

You do not need to install any third-party MCP server to view benchmark results. The committed `recording-stats.json` files contain aggregate metrics (token counts, record counts). Generate a comparison report with:

```bash
uv run agent-bench compare
```

To replay or validate recordings (which read the raw `recording.json` files), you must first record responses locally — raw recordings are gitignored and not committed.

### Capturing Fresh Recordings

The automated recorder script handles all native-mcp recordings. Set up your `.env` profile (see `.env.template`) and run:

```bash
uv run agent-bench record --path native-mcp --connectors linear,slack,zendesk,gong,salesforce --date 2026-04-30
```

This launches each connector's MCP server, executes the benchmark tool calls, and saves recordings in the standard format.

To record a single connector:

```bash
uv run agent-bench record --path native-mcp --connectors linear --date 2026-04-30
```

Stats are generated automatically after recording. To regenerate the comparison report:

```bash
uv run agent-bench compare --date 2026-04-30 --output artifacts/2026-04-30/comparison-report.md
```

To regenerate stats from existing recordings without re-recording:

```bash
uv run agent-bench record --path native-mcp --stats-only --date 2026-04-30
```

### Recording File Format

Each recording file is a JSON array of objects:

```json
[
  {
    "tool": "mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_issues",
    "args": {"query": "context store", "limit": 10},
    "wall_clock_ms": 0,
    "response": { ... }
  }
]
```

Some tasks (e.g., Slack list) produce multiple calls per recording file. Use `--reset` to start fresh or omit it to append additional calls.

---

## Gong MCP

The benchmark uses the community **kenazk/gong-mcp** server (TypeScript, local Node.js process) via stdio transport. No official Gong MCP server exists.

**Repo:** https://github.com/kenazk/gong-mcp

> **Note:** This package is not published to npm, so `npx` will not work. You must clone and build locally.

### Prerequisites

- Node.js 18 or later
- npm
- A Gong API access key and secret (see [Obtaining Gong API credentials](#obtaining-gong-api-credentials) below)

### Installation

Clone the repo and build:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/kenazk/gong-mcp.git
cd gong-mcp
npm install
npm run build
```

Verify the built entry point exists:

```bash
ls dist/index.js
```

### Obtaining Gong API credentials

Gong uses Basic authentication with an access key and secret. To generate them:

1. Sign in to Gong as an admin at https://app.gong.io
2. Go to **Company Settings** > **Ecosystem** > **API**
3. Click **Get API Key** (or manage existing keys)
4. Copy the **Access Key** and **Access Key Secret**

API keys are org-wide and require admin permissions to create. Each key pair has full read access to your Gong data.

### Environment Variables

Set these in your `.env` profile:

```bash
GONG_ACCESS_KEY=your-access-key
GONG_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET=[REDACTED]
# Absolute path to the dist/index.js you just built (required)
GONG_MCP_SERVER_PATH=/absolute/path/to/gong-mcp/dist/index.js
```

`GONG_MCP_SERVER_PATH` is required — there is no default. Set it to the absolute path of your local build.

If you store credentials in 1Password, these live under the `gong` item, section `test-credentials-basic`, fields `access_key` and `access_key_secret`. Run `agent-bench populate-env` to sync them to `.env`.

### Verifying credentials

Smoke-test the API credentials before running the full recording:

```bash
curl -s -u "$GONG_ACCESS_KEY:$GONG_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET" \
  https://api.gong.io/v2/calls?fromDateTime=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z | head -c 200
```

A successful response returns JSON with a `calls` array. A `401` means the credentials are invalid or revoked.

### How the Recording Script Launches It

The `GongMCP` class in `src/agent_bench/recording/native_mcp_recorder.py` spawns the Node.js process with stdio transport:

```bash
node "$GONG_MCP_SERVER_PATH"
```

The process reads JSON-RPC messages from stdin and writes responses to stdout. The access key and secret are passed via environment variables (`GONG_ACCESS_KEY`, `GONG_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET`).

### Available Tools

The upstream server exposes two tools:

| MCP Tool | Args | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `list_calls` | `{"fromDateTime": "...", "toDateTime": "..."}` | List calls with optional date range filtering |
| `retrieve_transcripts` | `{"callIds": ["..."]}` | Retrieve transcripts for one or more call IDs |

The benchmark uses `list_calls` for the `gong-search` scenario. Neither tool supports a single-call get-by-ID operation (the Gong REST API has `GET /v2/calls/{id}` but the MCP server does not wrap it), so `gong-get` is marked "Not Comparable".

Notable limitations:

- Gong's API has no keyword search. The `list_calls` tool lists calls by date range with a fixed page size of 100.
- No field selection; full call objects are always returned.
- `gong-get` is marked "Not Comparable" since native-mcp has no get-by-ID tool.
- `gong-search` uses date-range filtering on both paths (comparable).

## Comparison With Agent MCP

| Dimension | Third-Party MCP | Agent MCP (`agent-mcp`) |
|---|---|---|
| Servers | One per service (Linear, Slack, Zendesk, Gong, Salesforce) | Unified `integrations_connectors_id_execute` |
| Auth | Per-service (OAuth, bot tokens, or API keys) | Single Airbyte Cloud OAuth credential set |
| Field selection | Not available; full responses returned | `select_fields` narrows returned fields |
| Response shape | Varies by provider (JSON, text, markdown) | Uniform typed JSON envelope |
| Hosting | Remote (Linear, Slack, Salesforce) or local (Zendesk, Gong) | Airbyte-hosted proxy at `mcp.airbyte.ai` |

def test_scenario_loads_choreographed_format() -> None:
    gong_get = load_scenario("gong-get")
    assert gong_get.is_choreographed
    assert gong_get.paths is not None
    assert "agent-mcp" in gong_get.paths
    # gong-get has no native-mcp path — the upstream kenazk/gong-mcp server
    # has no get-by-ID tool, so this scenario is marked not-comparable.
    assert "native-mcp" not in gong_get.paths
    assert gong_get.is_comparable is False

    agent_calls = gong_get.paths["agent-mcp"].tool_calls
    assert len(agent_calls) == 1
    assert agent_calls[0].server == "airbyte-agent"
    assert agent_calls[0].tool == "integrations_connectors_id_execute"
    assert agent_calls[0].args["entity"] == "calls"
    assert agent_calls[0].args["action"] == "context_store_search"
    assert agent_calls[0].args["params"]["query"]["filter"]["eq"]["id"] == "1005803797056190704"
    assert agent_calls[0].args["params"]["limit"] == 1
    assert "id" in agent_calls[0].args["select_fields"]


def test_multi_step_scenario_loads() -> None:
    scenario = load_scenario("gong-to-salesforce-zendesk-lookup")
    assert scenario.is_choreographed
    assert len(scenario.paths["agent-mcp"].tool_calls) == 3
    assert len(scenario.paths["native-mcp"].tool_calls) == 3

    agent_calls = scenario.paths["agent-mcp"].tool_calls
    assert agent_calls[0].connector_id_env == "GONG_CONNECTOR_ID"
    assert agent_calls[1].connector_id_env == "SALESFORCE_CONNECTOR_ID"
    assert agent_calls[2].connector_id_env == "ZENDESK_CONNECTOR_ID"


def test_scenario_connectors_property() -> None:
    scenario = load_scenario("gong-to-salesforce-zendesk-lookup")
    connectors = scenario.connectors
    assert "gong" in connectors
    assert "salesforce" in connectors
    assert "zendesk" in connectors


def test_not_comparable_scenarios() -> None:
    slack_get = load_scenario("slack-get")
    assert slack_get.is_comparable is False

    slack_search = load_scenario("slack-search")
    assert slack_search.is_comparable is False

def test_agent_mcp_recording_parses_execution_metadata_latency(tmp_path) -> None:
    scenario = load_scenario("linear-get")
    rec_dir = tmp_path
    rec_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (rec_dir / "recording.json").write_text(json.dumps([{
        "tool": "mcp__airbyte-agent__execute",
        "args": {"items": [{
            "connector_id": "linear-id",
            "entity": "issues",
            "action": "get",
            "params": {"id": "issue-1"},
            "select_fields": ["id"],
        }]},
        "response": {"results": [{
            "result": {
                "status": "success",
                "result": {"id": "issue-1", "title": "One"},
                "execution_metadata": {"execution_time_ms": 123},
            },
        }]},
    }]))

    path = AgentMCPPath(_config(), rec_dir, mode="replay")
    result = _run_path(path, scenario)
    assert result.status == "ok"
    assert result.total_latency_ms == 123
    assert result.total_records == 1
    assert result.single_record_calls == 1
    assert result.single_record_tokens > 0



def test_context_store_search_passthrough() -> None:
    """context_store_search action passes params directly through."""
    task = Task(
        label="Get account via context store",
        action="context_store_search",
        entity="accounts",
        metric_focus="single_record_fetch",
        params={"query": {"filter": {"eq": {"Id": "001"}}}, "limit": 1},
    )
    dispatch = _DISPATCH["salesforce"]
    action, params = _translate(task, dispatch)
    assert action == "context_store_search"
    assert params["query"]["filter"]["eq"]["Id"] == "001"
    assert params["limit"] == 1


def _run_path(path: AgentMCPPath, scenario) -> BenchmarkResult:
    task = scenario.task
    if task is None:
        agent_call = scenario.paths["agent-mcp"].tool_calls[0]
        action = agent_call.args.get("action", "get")
        params = agent_call.args.get("params", {})
        inferred = scenario.inferred_action
        is_single_record = inferred == "get" or params.get("limit") == 1
        task = Task(
            label=f"{action} {agent_call.args.get('entity', 'unknown')}",
            action=action,
            entity=agent_call.args.get("entity", "unknown"),
            metric_focus="single_record_fetch" if is_single_record else "bulk_list",
            params=params,
        )

    async def collect() -> BenchmarkResult:
        result = None
        async for _step, current in path.run_task(task, scenario):
            result = current
        assert result is not None
        return result

    return asyncio.run(collect())

    )

"""Populate `.env` files from 1Password.

Reads the `.env.template` to discover which variables are declared, fetches
native-MCP connector credentials from the `direct-connector-credentials`
vault, and writes a ready-to-use `.env` file. Agent-MCP variables
(`AIRBYTE_ORGANIZATION_ID`, connector IDs, etc.) are left as-is if already
present in the output file, or blank for the user to fill in.

The recording layer (`native_mcp_recorder`, `agent_mcp_recorder`) never
touches 1Password directly — it reads `.env` only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path


REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
ENV_TEMPLATE = REPO_ROOT / ".env.template"
DEFAULT_ENV_PATH = REPO_ROOT / ".env"

VAULT = "direct-connector-credentials"

# Mapping from env var name → (1Password item, field, section).
# Only native-MCP credentials that live in 1Password are listed here.
_OP_FIELD_MAP: dict[str, tuple[str, str, str]] = {
    "LINEAR_API_KEY": ("linear", "api_key", "test-credentials-api-key"),
    "SLACK_USER_OAUTH_TOKEN": ("slack", "user_oauth_token", "test-credentials-mcp"),
    "GONG_ACCESS_KEY": ("gong", "access_key", "test-credentials-basic"),
    "GONG_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET": ("gong", "access_key_secret", "test-credentials-basic"),
    "SF_MCP_CONSUMER_KEY": ("salesforce", "consumer_key", "test-credentials-mcp"),
    "SF_MCP_CONSUMER_SECRET": ("salesforce", "consumer_secret", "test-credentials-mcp"),
    "SF_MCP_REFRESH_TOKEN": ("salesforce", "refresh_token", "test-credentials-mcp"),
    "ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN": ("zendesk-support", "subdomain", "test-credentials-oauth"),
    "ZENDESK_ACCESS_TOKEN": ("zendesk-support", "access_token", "test-credentials-oauth"),
}


def _resolve_op_token() -> str:
    """Return a 1Password service account token from the environment."""
    token = [REDACTED]"SONAR_CONNECTOR_CREDS_1PASS_TOKEN") or os.environ.get(
        "DEVIN_1PASSWORD_SERVICE_TOKEN", ""
    )
    if not token:
        raise EnvironmentError(
            "No 1Password token found. Set SONAR_CONNECTOR_CREDS_1PASS_TOKEN or "
            "DEVIN_1PASSWORD_SERVICE_TOKEN."
        )
    return token


def _fetch_op_item(item: str, op_token: str, cache: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
    """Fetch and cache a 1Password item's fields list.

    Returns the `fields` list from the item JSON. Subsequent calls for the
    same item name reuse the cached result.
    """
    if item in cache:
        return cache[item]

    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN"] = op_token

    cmd = [
        "op", "item", "get", item,
        f"--vault={VAULT}",
        "--format=json",
        "--reveal",
    ]
    print(f"  Fetching {item} from 1Password ...")
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)  # noqa: S603
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"`op item get {item}` failed: {result.stderr.strip()}")

    data = json.loads(result.stdout)
    fields = data.get("fields", [])
    cache[item] = fields
    return fields


def _extract_field(fields: list[dict], field: str, section: str) -> str:
    """Extract a field value from a cached 1Password fields list."""
    for f_entry in fields:
        f_section = (f_entry.get("section") or {}).get("label", "")
        f_label = f_entry.get("label", "")
        if f_label == field and f_section == section:
            return f_entry.get("value", "")
    return ""


def _parse_template(template_path: Path = ENV_TEMPLATE) -> list[str]:
    """Return the ordered list of env var names declared in `.env.template`."""
    names: list[str] = []
    for line in template_path.read_text().splitlines():
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
            continue
        key = stripped.split("=", 1)[0].strip()
        if key:
            names.append(key)
    return names


def _read_existing_env(env_path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Read an existing `.env` file into a dict, preserving decoded values.

    Uses python-dotenv's parser to ensure correct unescaping (e.g. `\\$` → `$`)
    so that re-writing through `_quote_value` doesn't double-escape.
    """
    from dotenv import dotenv_values

    if not env_path.is_file():
        return {}
    raw = dotenv_values(env_path)
    return {k: v for k, v in raw.items() if v is not None}


def _quote_value(value: str) -> str:
    """Wrap a value in quotes if it contains dotenv-sensitive chars."""
    if not value:
        return ""
    # Escape $ as \$ inside double quotes to prevent python-dotenv interpolation
    if "$" in value:
        escaped = value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("$", "\\$").replace("\n", "\\n")
        return f'"{escaped}"'
    needs_quoting = any(c in value for c in (" ", "#", "'", '"', "\n", "\t"))
    if needs_quoting:
        escaped = value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n")
        return f'"{escaped}"'
    return value


def populate_env(
    output_path: Path = DEFAULT_ENV_PATH,
    overwrite: bool = False,
) -> Path:
    """Fetch native-MCP credentials from 1Password and write a `.env` file.

    Variables already set in an existing `.env` are preserved unless
    `overwrite` is True. Agent-MCP variables not in 1Password are left
    blank for manual entry.

    Returns the path to the written file.
    """
    op_token = [REDACTED]
    template_vars = _parse_template()
    existing = {} if overwrite else _read_existing_env(output_path)

    lines = [
        "# Auto-generated by `agent-bench populate-env`.",
        "# Edit freely — this file is gitignored.",
        "",
    ]

    item_cache: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}

    for var in template_vars:
        # Keep existing value if present
        if var in existing and existing[var]:
            lines.append(f"{var}={_quote_value(existing[var])}")
            continue

        # Try 1Password lookup
        if var in _OP_FIELD_MAP:
            item, field, section = _OP_FIELD_MAP[var]
            fields = _fetch_op_item(item, op_token, item_cache)
            value = _extract_field(fields, field, section)
            if value:
                lines.append(f"{var}={_quote_value(value)}")
                print(f"  {var} ✓")
                continue

        # Not in 1Password or not found — leave blank
        lines.append(f"{var}=")

    output_path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    return output_path

"""Real-MCP client and OAuth handling for `mcp.airbyte.ai`. This module is what makes the Agent MCP path actually use MCP. It speaks JSON-RPC over Streamable HTTP to the hosted MCP server and uses the official MCP SDK's `OAuthClientProvider` for browser-based PKCE auth. Tokens persist to ``~/.airbyte/agent-mcp-tokens.json`` so subsequent runs refresh automatically. The refresh token has an approximately 60-day TTL; after it expires the user must re-auth in a browser. """ from __future__ import annotations import asyncio import json import os import socket import threading import time import warnings import webbrowser from dataclasses import dataclass from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer from pathlib import Path from typing import Any from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse import httpx from mcp.client.auth import OAuthClientProvider, TokenStorage from mcp.shared.auth import ( OAuthClientInformationFull, OAuthClientMetadata, OAuthToken, ) DEFAULT_MCP_URL = "https://mcp.airbyte.ai/mcp" DEFAULT_TOKEN_PATH = Path.home() / ".airbyte" / "agent-mcp-tokens.json" CLIENT_NAME = "airbyte-agents-benchmarks" class FileTokenStorage(TokenStorage): """Persist OAuth tokens + DCR client info to a single JSON file. Layout: { "client_info": {...OAuthClientInformationFull...}, "tokens": {...OAuthToken...} } """ def __init__(self, path: Path = DEFAULT_TOKEN_PATH) -> None: self.path = path def _read(self) -> dict: if not self.path.is_file(): return {} text = self.path.read_text() try: return json.loads(text) except json.JSONDecodeError: warnings.warn( f"Token file {self.path} is corrupted (invalid JSON). " "Starting with empty state. Re-run `agent-bench auth` to re-authenticate.", stacklevel=2, ) return {} def _write(self, data: dict) -> None: self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) self.path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2)) try: os.chmod(self.path, 0o600) except OSError: pass async def get_tokens(self) -> OAuthToken | None: raw = self._read().get("tokens") return OAuthToken.model_validate(raw) if raw else None async def set_tokens(self, tokens: OAuthToken) -> None: data = self._read() data["tokens"] = tokens.model_dump(mode="json") self._write(data) async def get_client_info(self) -> OAuthClientInformationFull | None: raw = self._read().get("client_info") return OAuthClientInformationFull.model_validate(raw) if raw else None async def set_client_info(self, client_info: OAuthClientInformationFull) -> None: data = self._read() data["client_info"] = client_info.model_dump(mode="json") self._write(data) def _free_port() -> int: with socket.socket() as s: s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)) return s.getsockname()[1] @dataclass class _CallbackResult: code: str | None = None state: str | None = None error: str | None = None def _make_callback_server(port: int, result: _CallbackResult, done: threading.Event) -> HTTPServer: class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_GET(self): # noqa: N802 params = parse_qs(urlparse(self.path).query) result.code = params.get("code", [None])[0] result.state = params.get("state", [None])[0] result.error = params.get("error", [None])[0] self.send_response(200) self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/html") self.end_headers() body = ( "

Authorization complete.

" "

You can close this tab and return to the terminal.

" if result.error is None else f"

Authorization failed: {result.error}

" ) self.wfile.write(body.encode()) done.set() def log_message(self, *args, **kwargs): # silence default stderr noise pass return HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), Handler) def make_oauth_provider( server_url: str = DEFAULT_MCP_URL, storage: TokenStorage | None = None, timeout_seconds: float = 300.0, ) -> OAuthClientProvider: """Build an OAuthClientProvider that drives a one-shot localhost browser flow. Picks a free localhost port, registers it as the redirect URI via DCR, opens the user's default browser, runs a single-request HTTP server to receive the callback, and returns the auth code to the SDK. """ storage = storage or FileTokenStorage() callback_port = _free_port() redirect_uri = f"http://127.0.0.1:{callback_port}/callback" client_metadata = OAuthClientMetadata( client_name=CLIENT_NAME, redirect_uris=[redirect_uri], grant_types=["authorization_code", "refresh_token"], response_types=["code"], token_endpoint_auth_method="none", ) async def redirect_handler(authorization_url: str) -> None: print(f"\nOpening browser to authenticate with {server_url} ...") print("If the browser does not open automatically, visit this URL:") print(f" {authorization_url}\n") webbrowser.open(authorization_url) async def callback_handler() -> tuple[str, str | None]: result = _CallbackResult() done = threading.Event() server = _make_callback_server(callback_port, result, done) thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True) thread.start() try: ready = await asyncio.get_event_loop().run_in_executor( None, done.wait, timeout_seconds ) finally: server.shutdown() server.server_close() if not ready: raise TimeoutError("Timed out waiting for OAuth redirect to localhost") if result.error or not result.code: raise RuntimeError(f"OAuth flow failed: {result.error or 'no code returned'}") return result.code, result.state return OAuthClientProvider( server_url=server_url, client_metadata=client_metadata, storage=storage, redirect_handler=redirect_handler, callback_handler=callback_handler, timeout=timeout_seconds, ) class AirbyteMCPClient: """Streamable HTTP MCP client for `mcp.airbyte.ai` with OAuth. Mirrors the shape of the LinearMCP / SalesforceMCP clients in `agent_bench.recording.native_mcp_recorder`: `initialize()` then `call_tool(name, args)` returning `(parsed_response, wall_clock_ms)`. The auth provider handles login + refresh transparently. """ def __init__( self, server_url: str = DEFAULT_MCP_URL, organization_id: str | None = None, storage: TokenStorage | None = None, ) -> None: self.server_url = server_url self.organization_id = organization_id self.auth = make_oauth_provider(server_url=server_url, storage=storage) self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(auth=self.auth, timeout=60.0) self._session_id: str | None = None self._next_id = 1 def _headers(self) -> dict[str, str]: h = { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream", } if self.organization_id: h["X-Organization-Id"] = self.organization_id if self._session_id: h["mcp-session-id"] = self._session_id return h async def initialize(self) -> None: init_req = { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": self._next_id, "method": "initialize", "params": { "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05", "capabilities": {}, "clientInfo": {"name": CLIENT_NAME, "version": "0.1"}, }, } self._next_id += 1 resp = await self._client.post( self.server_url, json=init_req, headers=self._headers() ) resp.raise_for_status() # Streamable HTTP returns the session id in the response header sid = resp.headers.get("mcp-session-id") if sid: self._session_id = sid # Send notifications/initialized to complete the handshake notif = { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized", "params": {}, } notif_resp = await self._client.post( self.server_url, json=notif, headers=self._headers() ) notif_resp.raise_for_status() async def call_tool( self, tool_name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any] ) -> tuple[Any, float]: req = { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": self._next_id, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": tool_name, "arguments": arguments}, } self._next_id += 1 t0 = time.perf_counter() resp = await self._client.post( self.server_url, json=req, headers=self._headers() ) wall_ms = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000 resp.raise_for_status() return _parse_jsonrpc_payload(resp.text), wall_ms async def close(self) -> None: await self._client.aclose() def _parse_jsonrpc_payload(text: str) -> Any: """Parse a Streamable HTTP MCP response (JSON or SSE) and return the inner tool result. The MCP server may return either ``application/json`` (plain JSON-RPC body) or ``text/event-stream`` (SSE-framed JSON-RPC). Tool results expose ``structuredContent`` (preferred) or a ``content[0].text`` blob that is itself a JSON string. """ candidates: list[dict] = [] stripped = text.strip() if stripped.startswith("{"): try: candidates.append(json.loads(stripped)) except json.JSONDecodeError: pass if not candidates: for line in text.split("\n"): if line.startswith("data:"): try: candidates.append(json.loads(line[5:].strip())) except json.JSONDecodeError: continue if not candidates: return {"error": "no parseable response", "raw": text} msg = next((c for c in candidates if "result" in c or "error" in c), candidates[0]) if "error" in msg and msg["error"]: return {"error": msg["error"]} result = msg.get("result", {}) if isinstance(result, dict): if "structuredContent" in result and result["structuredContent"] is not None: return result["structuredContent"] content = result.get("content") if isinstance(content, list) and content: text_blob = content[0].get("text", "") try: return json.loads(text_blob) except json.JSONDecodeError: return {"text": text_blob} return result

_DEFAULT_ARTIFACTS = FSPath(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "artifacts"


def _resolve_artifacts_dir(artifacts_dir: FSPath, date: str | None) -> FSPath:
    """Resolve the artifacts directory for a given date."""
    if date:
        return artifacts_dir / date
    if not artifacts_dir.is_dir():
        return artifacts_dir / datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    candidates = sorted(
        (d for d in artifacts_dir.iterdir() if d.is_dir() and d.name[0].isdigit()),
        reverse=True,
    )
    if candidates:
        return candidates[0]
    return artifacts_dir / datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")


REPORT_FILENAME = "comparison-report.md"
SYMLINK_DIR = FSPath(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "latest_comparison_report"


def _update_symlink(report_path: FSPath) -> None:
    """Point `latest_comparison_report/README.md` at the given report."""
    SYMLINK_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    link = SYMLINK_DIR / "README.md"
    target = FSPath(os.path.relpath(report_path, SYMLINK_DIR))
    if link.is_symlink() or link.exists():
        link.unlink()
    link.symlink_to(target)


@app.command()
def compare(
    artifacts_dir: FSPath = typer.Option(_DEFAULT_ARTIFACTS, "--artifacts-dir"),
    date: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--date", help="Artifact date folder (e.g. 2026-04-29). Defaults to latest."),
    left: str = typer.Option("agent-mcp", "--left", help="Left path slug for comparison"),
    right: str = typer.Option("native-mcp", "--right", help="Right path slug for comparison"),
    output: FSPath | None = typer.Option(None, "--output", "-o", help="Write markdown report to this file instead of the default location"),
    stdout: bool = typer.Option(False, "--stdout", help="Print report to stdout instead of writing to a file"),
) -> None:
    """Generate a markdown comparison report from recording-stats.json files.

    Compares token efficiency between two paths (default: agent-mcp vs native-mcp).
    Falls back to deriving stats from recording.json if stats files are absent.

    By default, writes the report to `<artifacts-dir>/<date>/comparison-report.md`
    and updates the `latest_comparison_report/README.md` symlink. Use `--stdout`
    to print instead, or `--output` to write to a custom path.
    """
    dated_dir = _resolve_artifacts_dir(artifacts_dir, date)
    if not dated_dir.is_dir():
        console.print(f"[red]Artifacts directory not found: {dated_dir}[/red]")
        raise typer.Exit(1)

    resolved_output = output or (None if stdout else dated_dir / REPORT_FILENAME)

    left_label = PATH_LABEL.get(left, left)
    right_label = PATH_LABEL.get(right, right)

    report = generate_comparison_report(
        artifacts_dir=dated_dir,
        left_path=left,
        right_path=right,
        left_label=left_label,
        right_label=right_label,
        output_path=resolved_output,
    )

    if resolved_output:
        console.print(f"[green]report →[/green] {resolved_output}")
        _update_symlink(resolved_output)
        console.print(f"[green]symlink →[/green] {SYMLINK_DIR / 'README.md'}")
    else:
        console.print(report)


@app.command(name="populate-env")
def populate_env_cmd(
    output: FSPath = typer.Option(DEFAULT_ENV_PATH, "--output", "-o", help="Path to write the .env file."),
    overwrite: bool = typer.Option(False, "--overwrite", help="Overwrite existing values instead of preserving them."),
) -> None:
    """Populate `.env` from 1Password credentials.

    Reads `.env.template` for the list of accepted variables, fetches
    native-MCP connector secrets from the `direct-connector-credentials`
    vault, and writes a `.env` file.  Agent-MCP variables not stored in
    1Password are left blank for manual entry.

    Existing values in the output file are preserved unless `--overwrite`
    is passed.
    """
    out = populate_env(output_path=FSPath(output), overwrite=overwrite)
    console.print(f"[green]Wrote {out}[/green]")


@app.command()
def auth(
    server_url: str = typer.Option(DEFAULT_MCP_URL, "--server-url", help="MCP server URL."),
    token_path: FSPath = typer.Option(DEFAULT_TOKEN_PATH, "--token-path", help="Path to persist OAuth tokens."),
) -> None:
    """One-time browser OAuth for `mcp.airbyte.ai`.

    Opens a browser, completes the PKCE flow, and persists the resulting
    access + refresh tokens. Re-run if you see 401 responses during recording.
    """
    load_dotenv()
    env_token_path = os.environ.get("AIRBYTE_TOKEN_PATH")
    if env_token_path and token_path == DEFAULT_TOKEN_PATH:
        token_path = FSPath(env_token_path)

    async def _auth() -> None:
        storage = FileTokenStorage(token_path)
        client = AirbyteMCPClient(server_url=server_url, storage=storage)
        try:
            await client.initialize()
        finally:
            await client.close()
        console.print(f"[green]Authenticated. Tokens saved to {token_path}.[/green]")

    try:
        asyncio.run(_auth())
    except httpx.ConnectError as exc:
        console.print(f"[red]Cannot reach MCP server at {server_url}: {exc}[/red]")
        raise typer.Exit(1) from None
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        console.print(f"[red]MCP server returned HTTP {exc.response.status_code}: {exc}[/red]")
        raise typer.Exit(1) from None
    except TimeoutError as exc:
        console.print(f"[red]{exc}[/red]")
        console.print("Ensure your browser completed the OAuth flow and the redirect reached localhost.")
        raise typer.Exit(1) from None


@app.command()
def record(
    path: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--path", help="Recording path: 'agent-mcp' or 'native-mcp'. Optional with --stats-only."),
    connectors: str = typer.Option("all", "--connectors", help="Comma-separated connector names, or 'all'."),
    date: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--date", help="Artifact date folder (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today (or latest for --stats-only)."),
    dry_run: bool = typer.Option(False, "--dry-run", help="Show what would be recorded without executing."),
    stats_only: bool = typer.Option(False, "--stats-only", help="Regenerate stats from existing recordings without re-recording."),
    emulated_mcp: bool = typer.Option(False, "--emulated-mcp/--no-emulated-mcp", help="Use Sonar REST API instead of real MCP (agent-mcp only)."),
    server_url: str = typer.Option(DEFAULT_MCP_URL, "--server-url", help="MCP server URL (agent-mcp, real MCP only)."),
    token_path: FSPath = typer.Option(DEFAULT_TOKEN_PATH, "--token-path", help="OAuth token path (agent-mcp, real MCP only)."),
) -> None:
    """Record MCP responses for benchmark replay.

    Captures live responses from either the Airbyte Agent MCP server or
    vendor-native MCP servers and writes them as recording artifacts.
    Automatically generates `recording-stats.json` after recording.

    Use `--stats-only` to regenerate stats from existing recordings
    without re-recording. In this mode `--path` is not required and
    `--date` defaults to the latest artifacts directory.
    """
    if stats_only:
        dated_dir = _resolve_artifacts_dir(_DEFAULT_ARTIFACTS, date)
        if not dated_dir.is_dir():
            console.print(f"[red]Artifacts directory not found: {dated_dir}[/red]")
            raise typer.Exit(1)
        count = write_stats_for_dir(dated_dir)
        if count:
            console.print(f"[green]Wrote {count} recording-stats.json file(s) in {dated_dir}[/green]")
        else:
            console.print(f"[red]No recording.json files found in {dated_dir}[/red]")
            raise typer.Exit(1)
        return

    if not path or path not in ("agent-mcp", "native-mcp"):
        console.print(f"[red]--path is required and must be 'agent-mcp' or 'native-mcp'.[/red]")
        raise typer.Exit(1)

    resolved_date = date or default_date()
    dated_dir = ARTIFACTS_ROOT / resolved_date
    connector_arg = None if connectors == "all" else connectors

    if path == "native-mcp":
        if emulated_mcp:
            console.print("[red]Emulated MCP is not available for native-mcp path.[/red]")
            raise typer.Exit(1)
        rc = record_native_mcp(connectors=connector_arg, date=resolved_date, dry_run=dry_run)

    elif emulated_mcp:
        rc = record_emulated_agent_mcp(connectors=connector_arg, date=resolved_date, dry_run=dry_run)

    else:
        rc = asyncio.run(
            record_agent_mcp(
                connectors=connector_arg,
                date=resolved_date,
                server_url=server_url,
                token_path=token_path,
                dry_run=dry_run,
            )
        )

    if rc != 0:
        console.print(f"[red]Recording failed (exit code {rc}). See errors above.[/red]")
        raise typer.Exit(rc)

    if dry_run:
        return

    if not dated_dir.is_dir():
        console.print(f"[yellow]No artifacts directory at {dated_dir} — skipping stats generation.[/yellow]")
        return

    count = write_stats_for_dir(dated_dir)
    if count:
        console.print(f"[green]Wrote {count} recording-stats.json file(s) in {dated_dir}[/green]")
    else:
        console.print(f"[yellow]No recording.json files found in {dated_dir}[/yellow]")


@app.command(name="record-one")
def record_one_cmd(
    path: str = typer.Option(..., "--path", help="Recording path: 'native-mcp' or 'agent-mcp'."),
    scenario: str = typer.Option(..., "--scenario", help="Scenario name, e.g. linear-search."),
    tool: str = typer.Option(..., "--tool", help="MCP tool name."),
    args: str = typer.Option(..., "--args", help="JSON string of tool arguments."),
    response_file: FSPath = typer.Option(..., "--response-file", help="Path to a file with the raw response JSON."),
    date: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--date", help="Artifact date folder (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today UTC."),
    wall_ms: float | None = typer.Option(None, "--wall-ms", help="Wall-clock ms. For agent-mcp, defaults to execution_metadata.execution_time_ms."),
    reset: bool = typer.Option(False, "--reset", help="Overwrite any existing recording for this scenario."),
) -> None:
    """Save a single MCP tool-call response as a benchmark recording."""
    if path not in ("native-mcp", "agent-mcp"):
        console.print(f"[red]Invalid --path {path!r}. Must be 'native-mcp' or 'agent-mcp'.[/red]")
        raise typer.Exit(1)

    date_str = date or default_date()
    out_path = record_one(
        path_slug=path,
        scenario=scenario,
        tool=tool,
        args_json=args,
        response_file=response_file,
        date=date_str,
        wall_ms=wall_ms,
        reset=reset,
    )
    existing = json.loads(out_path.read_text())
    console.print(f"saved -> {out_path} ({len(existing)} call(s))")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()

"""Protocol for benchmark paths."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import AsyncIterator, Protocol

from agent_bench.metrics import BenchmarkResult, StepResult
from agent_bench.scenarios.loader import Scenario, Task


class BenchmarkPath(Protocol):
    """Each path runs one task at a time and yields step-wise progress.

    A path is bound to one connector's scope at construction (auth + connector
    instance ID). The runner iterates over tasks and calls `run_task`.
    """

    name: str  # human-readable ("Agent MCP" | "Native MCP")
    short_name: str  # CLI slug ("agent-mcp" | "native-mcp")

    async def run_task(
        self, task: Task, scenario: Scenario
    ) -> AsyncIterator[tuple[StepResult, BenchmarkResult]]:
        """Yield (step_just_completed, running_total) after each step."""
        ...

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Release any HTTP clients / connector handles."""
        ...
